note: Q4 rebuild of stick04: same script, voice, acting and camera; every level is a dense, specific place (Halden street, park on a Saturday, a real classroom, the street at rush hour, the square with a rock stage, a lived-on volcano island, the bank's street) and every effect happens in the world: real signposts, a tripod sound meter, chalk on the blackboard, speaker stacks, dust shocks, an eruption with debris, shattering glass. Floating text is the label budget: LOUD!, PAIN!, CANNON FIRE?! (3). stick06: combined kit; every line carries Q2 body acting in `act`. stick07 (forensic fixes): no floating text (LOUD!/PAIN! dropped, CANNON FIRE? is a police report board); planned shots open establishing; acts dissolve; own light per act.

lines.see: On a busy Halden street a blast bursts the shop window behind Kai, splits the pavement in red-hot cracks and whips dust and leaves over the pavement (LOUD!), five real speaker stacks rise one after another under a hanging 5 LEVELS sign, then a 3,000 MI signpost rises behind Kai.
In the busy park Wren whispers: little breath puffs drift into Kai's ear, a LEVEL 1 signpost stands behind them, and a tripod sound meter pops up and reads 30 dB.
In a real classroom Kai talks to Bram under a hanging LEVEL 2 sign, the tripod meter reads 60 dB, then chalk on the blackboard draws 70 dB's bar ten times taller and writes 10x POWER!
Kai stands in the road at rush hour: a car's honk blasts dust and litter at him, its exhaust smokes, the meter reads 85 dB beside the LEVEL 3 post, and steam pours out of his sore ear.

In Halden square a rock stage fires sparks, the crowd fist-pumps, the wall of sound blows dust over the square, the meter reads 120 dB and Kai, ears steaming, is hit by PAIN! Red cracks race over the paving under him.

A lived-on volcano island (huts, boats, a lighthouse) with a KRAKATOA 1883 signpost; glowing lava cracks split the cone, then it explodes in a fireball, flinging rocks and lava sparks, an ash column rising.
Closer on the erupting volcano: a white ring of foam races out over the sea, the big tripod meter on the beach reads 170 dB, and a 100 MI HEARD IT signpost rises.

On the bank's street the police chief by his car gets a 3,000 MI FROM KRAKATOA signpost, the bang arrives: dust whips his feet, the bank stone cracks and its door glass bursts into shards, and he says CANNON FIRE?!
